body:
Dear OPM 68,

As you head home and begin to reflect on your OPM journey, we have one final ask if you haven’t done this already.

The program evaluation is your opportunity to “close the loop”—to capture what mattered, what challenged you, and what should endure for those who follow you. Many OPM participants tell us this moment of reflection is surprisingly meaningful.

We review every response in the coming days and use them directly to shape the future of OPM. Your perspective, right now, carries a weight it won’t have later.

When you have 10–15 minutes during your travel today, we’d be grateful if you completed the evaluation . Please do so in one sitting; the survey saves progress only while your browser remains open.

We’re aiming to hear from every member of OPM 68. We currently have heard from only 28% of you, and your voice is an important part of that collective picture.

We wish you safe travels back home and look forward to welcoming you to campus for Unit 2.

Warmly,
Ani, Josh, Patrick, Bernadette, and Esther

body:
The Morning: Pool problems

Plus, Iran, Japan and a $250 bill.

 View in browser | nytimes.com

May 29, 2026

By Sam Sifton

 Good morning. The United States and Iran say they are closing in on a deal . Japan’s population is plummeting . And my colleagues talked to Olivia Rodrigo. I’m going to start today, though, in the pool.

 In Washington. Allison Robbert for The New York Times

 Pool problems

 There are many surprising things to learn about the current renovation of the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. For one thing, the company doing the repairs didn’t have to bid for the job, and it’s receiving a puffed-up profit margin , according to my colleague David Fahrenthold, an investigative journalist in our Washington bureau.

 Federal construction projects like this one generally yield a profit of 6 to 12 percent, according to a National Park Service analysis that David obtained. The estimate from the firm fixing the reflecting pool yields 20 percent. That added at least $850,000 to the cost.

 Of course, it’s a difficult job. The pool is 167 feet wide and over 2,000 feet long. The water within it could fill roughly a half dozen Olympic-size swimming pools. And President Trump wants everything done in time for the celebration of America’s 250th birthday in July.

 The government thought the firm deserved extra for hustling. The cost they eventually settled on: $13.1 million, some seven times the amount the president initially said it would cost. That included the 20 percent profit margin and an additional 20 percent for “overhead,” which the Park Service analysis said “appears excessive.”

 The documents David obtained show something else, too: The contractor’s attempts earlier this month to seal gaps in the pool’s bottom failed, compelling the company and the Park Service to grasp for new solutions. And the waterproof paint it’s using on the bottom of the pool — “American Flag blue” — has bubbled or developed small holes in some places. Uneven spraying has left some areas with different shades of blue.

 Same as it ever was

 In the early 1920s. Bettmann Archive, via Getty Images

 Those problems may come as no surprise to anyone who owns a pool. Think of the upkeep and the ongoing costs: chemicals, pumps, cleaning, draining, covering, uncovering, filling, filtering, repeat. Something’s always going wrong. I have a friend with a pool. (Beats having a pool.) I asked him about it. He was forceful: “ It’s a lot .”

 Similarly, the reflecting pool has been a headache for the federal government almost from its start, in 1922. Contractors built a cavity for the pool, but their construction soon settled into the muddy wetlands below it. The water burbled under the harsh sun of Washington summers, growing murky as algae bloomed. And, yes, it leaked — eventually some 16 million gallons of water per year.

 In 2010, the Obama administration drained the pool and embarked on an expensive two-year renovation meant to seal the leaks and improve the filtration system. I found a Times article that ran right after it reopened in the fall of 2012. The first sentence may sound familiar: “The National Park Service has again drained the reflecting pool in front of the Lincoln Memorial to clean an algae buildup that formed after a $34 million overhaul.”

 THE LATEST NEWS

Politics

 At the White House. Evan Vucci/Reuters

 Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his agency had designed a $250 bill bearing Trump’s image . Congress would need to approve the currency.

 The Pentagon announced a $9.7 billion contract with Dell. Trump, who bought more than $1 million in Dell stock this year, stands to benefit.

 “Both parties kind of get it wrong”: Many Gen Z men who voted for Trump say they’re disappointed by his time in office. But they haven’t heard an appealing pitch from Democrats, either.

 A divided Supreme Court sided with a death row inmate from Mississippi . The inmate, who is Black, accused the white prosecutor in his case of illegally striking potential Black jurors from the panel that heard his case.

Israel

 Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel would expand its military control to 70 percent of Gaza , further squeezing Hamas.

 Israel will sever ties with the U.N. secretary general after being blacklisted over the alleged sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees.

War in the MIddle East

 The U.S. and Iran are moving closer to an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while they negotiate over the fate of Iran’s nuclear program, officials from both countries said.

 Trump announced that a U.S.-Iran peace deal would be contingent on a host of Middle Eastern countries establishing relations with Israel. Many of those countries were baffled by the demand.

Around the World

 In Romania , a Russian drone hit an apartment building , officials said. NATO condemned “Russia’s recklessness.”

 In Austria , a man was sentenced to 15 years in prison for plotting a terrorist attack at a Taylor Swift concert in Vienna.

Business

 U.S. consumer prices are rising at their fastest pace in years, according to inflation data from the Commerce Department.

 Anthropic has surpassed OpenAI as the most valuable artificial intelligence company .

 Bari Weiss, the editor in chief of CBS News, is overhauling “60 Minutes.” She fired two on-air correspondents and hired Nick Bilton, a former New York Times tech columnist, to run the show.

Other Big Stories

 A rocket built by Blue Origin, the Jeff Bezos-owned space company, blew up on the launchpad last night, sending a tower of flames into the sky. Bezos said no one was hurt. See a video .

 The F.B.I. arrested a C.I.A. official after investigators found $40 million worth of gold bars in his house .

 Rescuers in Alaska are racing to reach four climbers who fell near the 18,200-foot level of Mount McKinley.

 LIVES LIVED

 Happy in 2018. Bebeto Matthews/Associated Press

 Happy, an Asian elephant who had delighted Bronx Zoo visitors since the 1970s, died this week at 55. She was euthanized after a period of hospice care, prompted by a recent deterioration in her health.

 Happy was a particularly brilliant pachyderm. In the 2000s, she touched an X marked on her head with her trunk while looking in a mirror, acing a test of self-awareness that only humans, apes and dolphins had previously passed. That set off a legal fight from an animal rights group, which argued that confinement in a zoo was inhumane for a creature of such intellect.

 Read her obituary .

 OPINIONS

 Sandeep Vaheesan and Claire Kelloway say Americans can save on groceries if the country carves up Big Beef .

 Andrew Weissmann , a former general counsel of the F.B.I., has suggestions for how to stop Trump’s vindictive prosecutions .

 Here’s a column by M. Gessen on Viktor Orban’s defeat .

 Morning readers: Save on the complete Times experience.

 Experience all of The Times, all in one subscription — all with this introductory offer . You’ll gain unlimited access to news and analysis, plus games, recipes, product reviews and more.

 MORNING READS

 Al Torreggiani

 Agentic agent: A journalist tried to sell his home with the help of a chatbot. He beat the market .

 Hand to God: A Florida sheriff’s deputy pulled over a woman for holding a phone in her right hand, but she has no right hand.

 Genetic testing: What happens when your employer knows the diseases you might get?

 Your pick: Yesterday’s most clicked story in The Morning was about three questions that can help solve a stressful situation .

 TODAY’S NUMBER

 9th

 — That is the finishing position of the decathlete Russ Hodge at the 1964 Summer Olympics in Tokyo. His mother, the high jumper Alice Arden, finished in the same position at the 1936 Berlin Games. They were the first mother and son to have competed for the United States in the Olympics. Hodge died this month at 86 .

 SPORTS

 N.H.L.: Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion and one of the fiercest playoff performers in the league’s history, died, the NHL Alumni Association said. He was 60 .

 N.B.A.: The Western Conference finals are headed to a seventh game after the San Antonio Spurs defeated the Oklahoma City Thunder 118-91 in Game 6. Victor Wembanyama scored 28 points.

 French Open: Jannik Sinner, the world No. 1 and winner of 30 straight matches, lost in a shocking upset to Juan Manuel Cerúndolo of Argentina. Sinner was up two sets and serving for the match when the 90-degree Paris heat apparently took a toll on him .

 RECIPE OF THE DAY

 David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.

 If you can get your hands on some wild salmon this weekend, use it in Melissa Clark’s lovely recipe for a grilled salmon salad with lime, chiles and herbs . If you can’t, use chicken instead. Maybe it’s just me, but I taste desperation in the farmed fish — these animals meant to swim thousands of miles from rivers to ocean and back again but raised, instead, in a pen. The wild ones taste of freedom.

 THE ODD COUPLE

 Hannah Einbinder and Jean Smart Chantal Anderson for The New York Times

 Jean Smart came to an interview with The Times wearing a crisp merlot suit, gold hoop earrings and a swirly updo. Hannah Einbinder had arrived before her, in ripped jeans and a shirt that read “Planet Earth: Love It or Leave It.” Smart saw her. She narrowed her lips exactly as she does on “Hacks,” their HBO Max comedy, which ended last night. “I see you dressed,” she said coolly.

 The conversation that followed is a delightful read , though I must warn you that there are spoilers within it.

 More on culture

 The annual list of the 50 Best North American restaurants was released. Smyth in Chicago was named No. 1.

 A villanelle is an elaborate sort of poem, with complicated guidelines and only two end rhymes allowed. A.O. Scott, in another one of his lively, fascinating close reads, walks us through an excellent one, “Some Rules,” by Wendy Cope. Mind the unk and ind . You’ll learn a lot .

 The case for ugly-cool wraparound sunglasses . “They are so anti-fashion that they tip over into fashion,” writes Jacob Gallagher, whose job is to notice things like that.

 Late night hosts joked about President Trump’s low approval rating .

 SHOULD NOVELS GET UPDATES?

 Publishers have “modernized” novels for years, updating older cultural references and technologies to make them more palatable for younger readers. Some folks don’t like that . Check out the comments on the article.

 When Huck Finn gets on a hydrofoil to go down the Mississippi, we'll know the practice has gone too far.

 THE MORNING RECOMMENDS

 Caroline Tompkins for The New York Times

 Watch Olivia Rodrigo . The pop star visited “Popcast” this week to talk about superstardom, rivalries, jealousies, politics, songwriting and, above all, love.

 Protect yourself from the sun with guidance from the zinc-nosed ray-avoiders at Wirecutter.

 Jam out to the Toy Factory Project, “ Fire on the Mountain .”

 Take our news quiz .

 GAMES

 Here is today’s Spelling Bee . Yesterday’s pangram was unjamming .

 And here are today’s Mini Crossword , Wordle , Connections , Crossplay and Strands .

 Thanks for spending part of your morning with The Times and me. See you tomorrow. — Sam

body:
**Ethical Use of AI in Research and Writing: Strengthening Trust in the Age of Generative AI**
=============================================================================================

The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in research, writing, and communication is reshaping how organizations produce and share information across global operations.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

While generative AI tools deliver significant gains in speed and productivity, they also introduce a critical challenge: ensuring that AI-assisted outputs remain accurate, verifiable, and ethically produced.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

For BPOs and enterprises operating in highly regulated and reputation-sensitive environments, the integrity of AI-generated content is now directly tied to client trust, compliance readiness, and operational credibility.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As AI adoption accelerates, organizations must address how AI tools are used, as well as how secure and reliable is the digital infrastructure that supports it.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

####**The Emerging Risk: Information Integrity in AI Workflows**

As AI becomes embedded in everyday business communication, organizations are increasingly exposed to risks such as
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Inaccurate or fabricated AI-generated information
- Loss of source traceability in research and reporting
- Unverified use of AI-generated summaries in decision-making
- Unclear accountability in AI-assisted writing workflows.
These challenges highlight the need for adhering to ethical standards in AI-assisted knowledge production.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

####****A Unified Front for Ethical AI Adoption****

At the Asian Institute of Journalism and Communication (AIJC), one of the founding organizations of the Trusted Network Alliance (TNA), its long-standing advocacy for media and information literacy has expanded to include the ethical use of AI tools in communication.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

AIJC believes in this core principle: AI supports efficiency, but human judgment safeguards trust. Through its master’s programs, the AIJC Graduate School equips professionals with practical skills to ensure accuracy, transparency, and accountability in research, writing, and various forms of communication, including work assisted by artificial intelligence.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

With its programs’ emphasis on verification, critical thinking, and ethical boundaries in the use of generative AI tools, the Graduate School conducted the **AIJC Teaser Lecture on “Academic Integrity and AI in Research” and Virtual Open House** featuring Dr. Pauline Gidget Estella on May 20.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

####********Trusted Infrastructure for Responsible AI********

As organizations scale AI adoption, ethical practice must be supported by secure and resilient digital infrastructure.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

NOW Corporation, as a founding member of the Trusted Network Alliance, underscores that trusted communication depends not only on responsible use, but also on secure and reliable connectivity.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

End-to-end network security, data protection, and resilient systems remain essential foundations for ensuring integrity in AI-enabled operations.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

As organizations increasingly rely on AI-driven platforms and cloud-based collaboration tools, NOW Corporation continues to advocate for secure, high-reliability digital ecosystems that support responsible innovation. Through its focus on connectivity, cybersecurity, and resilient communications infrastructure, NOW emphasizes that trusted AI adoption depends not only on ethical human practices, but also on the strength and integrity of the networks that enable digital operations.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Together, AIJC and NOW emphasize that trusted AI adoption requires both human capability and secure digital infrastructure.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

####********Looking Ahead********

As generative AI becomes embedded in enterprise workflows, ethical competence in research and writing is emerging as a core operational requirement. Organizations that institutionalize ethical AI practices are better positioned to strengthen client trust and maintain communication integrity.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Trusted Network Alliance remains committed to advancing both the capability and infrastructure required for trusted, AI-enabled operations.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Trusted Network Alliance (TNA), formed by NOW Telecom and the Asian Institute of Journalism and Communication (AIJC), was launched in 2024 to strengthen cybersecurity measures for critical infrastructure in the Philippines.

Registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), TNA aims to drive the adoption of trusted networks for national development. It positions itself as a key force in enhancing collaboration and innovation across multiple industries to ensure the security and resilience of vital systems.

TNA is anchored in the U.S. Government’s adoption of the Zero Trust Architecture Framework, which aims to strengthen cybersecurity by shifting from a perimeter-based security model to one that verifies and authorizes every access request regardless of the network location.

**Trusted Ecosystem and Technology Partners**

Aligned with global efforts to create a safer and more secure digital landscape, TNA’s core mission is to foster collaboration among industry leaders, cybersecurity experts, and like-minded organizations. Through strategic partnerships, the alliance aims to enhance the security of the country’s digital ecosystem, promoting trusted technologies and solutions that help secure critical infrastructure.

TNA will serve as a hub for knowledge exchange, ensuring that organizations are prepared to tackle the evolving cybersecurity landscape while also driving innovation and digital transformation.

To reinforce its credibility and trustworthiness, TNA is building an ecosystem of renowned technology partners, including CISCO and Fortinet. This partnership network underscores TNA's commitment to integrating industry-leading solutions and expertise to protect and enhance critical infrastructure resilience across the Philippines and the Indo-Pacific region.

Since its inception, TNA has successfully brought together over 120 companies nationwide to engage in meaningful discussions, share insights on common challenges, and collaborate on future opportunities. Participants have come from various sectors, including government, finance, healthcare, telecommunications, and utilities.

**Trusted Technologies in the Indo-Pacific Region**

TNA is integral to NOW’s broader strategic vision of deploying a nationwide 5G mobile network and broadband infrastructure built on trusted technologies. This vision is bolstered by NOW Telecom’s partnership with the U.S. Government, highlighted during the White House announcements at the May 2024 Trilateral Meeting between the U.S., the Philippines, and Japan and the G7 White House Announcement on Cyber Digital Cooperation.

The partnership between NOW Telecom and the U.S. Government emphasizes the commitment to promoting trusted technologies and ensuring the security of critical infrastructure in the Indo-Pacific region.
